scenario.name: Unit 42 & CISA — Scattered Spider (Muddled Libra): SSO MFA Fatigue, RMM & AWS/ESXi Pivot
scenario.shortSubtitle: Palo Alto Unit 42 / CISA AA23-320A · Okta Identity Takeover, FleetDeck RMM & Cloud SAML Pivot
scenario.overview: Picture a sunlit grand hotel lobby with a polished marble concierge desk, a golden wall of numbered room-key hooks, velvet luggage carts, and brass elevator doors. Stepping up to the grand hotel concierge desk, a guest writes a cleverly worded forwarding note inside the open leather guestbook ledger. In this real-world scenario, the intruder steps up to the front-desk guestbook counter blending in with everyday guests, then moves quietly past the front-desk guestbook counter into neighboring restricted rooms. The hotel switchboard call log catches an unexpected outside phone call triggered directly from a routine guestbook check-in entry. In this scenario (T1078.004, Unit 42 & CISA, Scattered Spider (Muddled Libra): SSO MFA Fatigue, RMM & AWS/ESXi Pivot), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: helpdesk Social Engineering to Register, then logging Into the SSO Dashboard, Harvesting, then federation / Cloud Control-Plane Takeover. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Helpdesk Social Engineering to Register, then Logging Into the SSO Dashboard, Harvesting, then Federation / Cloud Control-Plane Takeover, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1/22 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: OKTA MFA PUSH FATIGUE & ROGUE DEVICE ENROLLMENT
stages.subtitle: Social engineering & MFA bombing leading to user.mfa.factor.activate
stages.description: Stepping up to the grand hotel concierge desk, a guest writes a cleverly worded forwarding note inside the open leather guestbook ledger. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder steps up to the front-desk guestbook counter blending in with everyday guests while everyday visitors and the hotel concierge go about their routine. Having gathered a target IT or DevOps engineer’s personal details (employee ID, date of birth, and manager name from LinkedIn or data brokers), the attacker calls the corporate IT Helpdesk impersonating that employee ("vishing", voice phishing) and claims they just got a new phone and lost their authenticator app. Persuaded by the caller, the helpdesk clerk triggers an administrative MFA reset (user.mfa.factor.activate, registering the attacker’s own smartphone or FIDO2 security key directly onto the employee’s Okta / Entra ID account so the attacker can approve their own MFA prompts at will). Unlike phishing attacks that try to steal a temporary session cookie, social-engineering the IT Helpdesk to enroll a new MFA factor on the Identity Provider (IdP) gives the attacker a permanent, legitimate MFA credential tied to their own device. In the documented Okta SystemLog exchange from Muddled Libra (UNC3944) to Core Identity & VLAN Switch, Core Identity & VLAN Switch responds with RESP Okta MFA (confirming that the MFA FACTOR ENROLL request succeeded on Core Identity & VLAN Switch and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 AUTHORIZED RMM TOOL DEPLOYMENT (SCREENCONNECT / NGROK)). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ MFA FACTOR ENROLL / ⇠#1 RESP Okta MFA) from Node ① (#1 Muddled Libra (UNC3944)) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Prisma Cloud & SIEM).

stages.title: AUTHORIZED RMM TOOL DEPLOYMENT (SCREENCONNECT / NGROK)
stages.subtitle: Living-off-the-land persistence via legitimate remote management binaries
stages.description: When the helpful hotel concierge reads that line aloud and phones the unlisted number written in the guestbook, the stranger on the line dictates fresh room-access orders. Here in Step 2 inside the grand hotel, the intruder moves quietly past the front-desk guestbook counter into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the penthouse private safe. Using the newly hijacked Single Sign-On (SSO) account, the attacker logs into the company’s virtual desktop (Citrix / Azure VDI), searches internal IT documentation (Confluence / SharePoint, documented by Mandiant UNC3944 as the primary way the group locates VPN guides, CyberArk/PAM instructions, and VMware vCenter architecture diagrams), and installs commercial Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) or mesh-VPN tools like AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, Tailscale, or ngrok (chosen because these tools are digitally signed by legitimate software vendors so antivirus does not block them, and they maintain an encrypted outbound tunnel that survives even if the victim’s SSO password and MFA are later reset). Commercial RMM agents establish persistent outbound TLS/WebSocket connections to the vendor’s relay cloud, giving the attacker full interactive desktop control without deploying any custom malware binary. In the documented Sysmon EID 1 exchange from Core Identity & VLAN Switch to Okta / Entra ID SSO Portal, Okta / Entra ID SSO Portal responds with ACK PID 7488 (confirming that the RMM SCREENCONNECT request succeeded on Okta / Entra ID SSO Portal and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 SAML FEDERATION PIVOT TO AWS & VMWARE VCENTER). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ RMM SCREENCONNECT / ⇠#2 ACK PID 7488) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 Okta / Entra ID SSO Portal), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Prisma Cloud & SIEM).

stages.title: SAML FEDERATION PIVOT TO AWS & VMWARE VCENTER
stages.subtitle: AssumeRoleWithSAML into AWS Production + CreateAccessKey & ESXi SSH
stages.description: Following the caller’s instructions, the concierge hands over a brass master room key from the back rack and unlocks the private elevator floor. In this final step inside the grand hotel, the intruder moves quietly past the front-desk guestbook counter into neighboring restricted rooms until the hotel switchboard call log catches the mismatch. Combining Unit 42’s and Mandiant’s findings: pivoting through the SSO dashboard into the AWS / Azure cloud management console, the attacker invokes sts:AssumeRole (minting temporary high-privilege cloud credentials) and calls CreateSAMLProvider / UpdateAssumeRolePolicy (registering a second, attacker-controlled SAML Identity Provider inside the cloud tenant, acting as a "golden SAML" backdoor that lets the attacker mint Admin cloud sessions even after the corporate Okta/Entra tenant is locked down). Simultaneously, for on-premises infrastructure, they add their compromised account to the Active Directory ESX Admins group to take direct SSH control over VMware ESXi hypervisors and export production S3 buckets. By compromising the Single Sign-On and Active Directory identity layer that governs both cloud role federation and hypervisor authentication, the attacker moves straight from a phone call to the IT Helpdesk into full control of AWS/Azure and VMware ESXi without touching a single network firewall exploit. In the documented CloudTrail STS/IAM exchange from Okta / Entra ID SSO Portal to Admin Endpoint (RMM Persistence), Admin Endpoint (RMM Persistence) responds with RESP AKIA...Key (confirming that the ASSUMEROLE + KEY request succeeded on Admin Endpoint (RMM Persistence) and completing the final execution objective of Unit 42 & CISA, Scattered Spider (Muddled Libra): SSO MFA Fatigue, RMM & AWS/ESXi Pivot). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ ASSUMEROLE + KEY / ⇠#3 RESP AKIA...Key) from Node ③ (#3 Okta / Entra ID SSO Portal) to Node ④ (#4 Admin Endpoint (RMM Persistence)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Prisma Cloud & SIEM).

detectionRule.title: Okta New MFA Factor Enrolled After Push Fatigue Burst
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Okta Suspicious MFA Factor Enrollment
logsource:
  product: okta
  service: okta
detection:
  selection:
    eventType:
      - 'user.mfa.factor.activate'
      - 'user.mfa.factor.update'
    outcome.result: 'SUCCESS'
  condition: selection
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Enforce phishing-resistant FIDO2/WebAuthn (Okta FastPass with number matching / device-bound keys) and require identity verification out-of-band before helpdesk MFA resets.

detectionRule.title: Unauthorized RMM Agent Execution (CISA AA23-320A Scattered Spider)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Suspicious Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) Execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
      - '\fleetdeck_agent.exe'
      - '\AnyDesk.exe'
      - '\ngrok.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
detectionRule.mitigation: Block unapproved RMM domains at the firewall/DNS layer and enforce application allowlisting for remote support binaries.

detectionRule.title: Federated SAML Session Creating Permanent AWS IAM Access Keys
detectionRule.ruleCode:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventSource == "iam.amazonaws.com" and EventName == "CreateAccessKey"
| where UserIdentityType == "AssumedRole" and UserIdentityPrincipalId has "@"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIpAddress, UserIdentityArn, RequestParameters
detectionRule.mitigation: Apply AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) prohibiting long-lived IAM Access Key creation and isolate VMware vCenter/ESXi management interfaces from standard SSO tiers.
